scope: Two local batcher recovery checks for the l1-null-receipts case; full distributed equivalence remains unproven.
fault_proof: The actual second post reaches the Anvil mempool while mining is disabled; spool retains block 2 and durable cursor remains at block 1.
The healthy endpoint sees the mined receipt and logs; the faulted endpoint returns a null receipt and no settlement logs.
The first actor finishes while the null-receipt fault remains active. Disabling receipt-error reconciliation exposes the actual null-response error.
The second actor is cancelled before mining. Restart succeeds while faults remain active and the indexer never answers; replay of covered block 2 and new block 3 yields exactly three total posts.
implementation: Extract unchanged production feed construction into a private L1Side method used by run_once and the fixture. Preserve defaults, argument values and side-effect order. Add only a dev-dependency on the existing fault-proxy crate.
invariants: No durable progress for an unmined post
Exact canonical batch indices and L2 ranges
DA certificates resolve payloads that reconstruct to the exact block and cursor
No duplicate L1 sends or nonce gaps
Startup does not wait for the unavailable indexer

batcher_library.note: The two new ignored checks are executed explicitly by the component runner.

validation.style: just style passes; the existing proc-macro-error2 future-incompatibility notice remains.

negative_control_details.ignore_contract_coverage: Replay posts covered block 2 twice; durable last_batch_index is 4 instead of 3.
negative_control_details.premature_cursor: The cursor advances to the unmined second post and violates the exact disk assertion.
negative_control_details.ignore_receipt_reconciliation: The real sender reports: await postBatch receipt: server returned a null response when a non-null response was expected.

limits: No follower fleet, alert, Nomad, consensus-retention or distributed DA proof.
The tests use deterministic mining and cancellation, not expiry of the unchanged 120-second receipt timeout. Alloy combines Tokio polling with wall-clock timeout bookkeeping.
The provider poll interval is 10 ms only in the fixture.
The reused local DA server serves until the test process exits.
No transaction performance claim or product defect established.
Payloads contain empty boundary blocks; no transaction-execution or full-chain transfer-progress claim.
